Subject: Operational recovery assertion and RTO/RPO evidence request

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Arcadia Health's due diligence for our integration pilots, our security team is consolidating evidence around Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery. We need to collect artifacts and short answers that map to the SOC 2/CAIQ questions under the BCP/DR category. Specific asks: 

- A short runbook overview (who does what on primary detection, failover, and restore).
- Measured RTO/RPO results from an actual test or production incident (timestamps, measured durations, impacted services).
- Tabletop exercise notes and attendee list from the last 12 months.
- A copy or export of any failover run logs (sanitized is fine) and snapshots referenced in those logs.

Can you provide these items, or point me to a secured folder where we can retrieve them? We have a third-party auditor copying this thread (audits@thirdparty-audit.com) and would like materials by COB Nov 28 if possible.

Also — for context — please include any caveats about services with best-effort recovery (e.g., eventual consistency windows, async replication limitations).

Thanks,

Maria Lopez
Sr. Security Program Manager
Arcadia Health

Maria —

Appreciate the clear list. We can provide the requested artifacts. I've attached the primary items we typically share for BCP/DR evidence and will surface a few more items from engineering after an internal run of the retrieval process:

- RI-DR-Runbook-v1.4.pdf (runbook executive summary + escalation matrix)
- RTO-RPO-Matrix-20261015.xlsx (service-level measured RTO/RPO per region/service)
- Tabletop-Exercise-Notes-20261015.txt (attendees, scenario, outcomes)

Quick notes up front: our serving runtime uses asynchronous KV replication for LRU caches; full KV-state restore is typically sub-minute for recent keys but can be best-effort for historical cold keys — we'll call that out explicitly in the matrix. For critical metadata we maintain multi-AZ synchronous writes with an observed RPO < 5 minutes in our last planned failover. Our measured end-to-end read-availability RTO for primary model serving (including rolling restart + cache warm) from the Oct 15 test was ~12 minutes (see matrix).

Action items I will take this week:
- Marissa: pull the raw failover run logs and sanitize any customer identifiers.
- Neha: confirm timestamps and attach the snapshot exports for the KV store and metadata DB.
- Karthik: validate any configuration caveats for Private deployments we should call out (VPC, on-prem variations).

Can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough the week of Nov 29? I can walk Arcadia's security team and your auditor through the artifacts line-by-line.

Thanks —
Priyom
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Maria / Arcadia team —

Confirmed for Tue Dec 1, 10:00 AM PST. Calendar invite sent (should arrive shortly). We uploaded the sanitized artifacts and added short annotated notes for the auditor. Links and a short explanation are below: 

Drive folder (read-only link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Redwood-DR
Contents uploaded (sanitized):
- RI-DR-Runbook-v1.4.pdf — executive runbook + escalation matrix.
- RTO-RPO-Matrix-20261015.xlsx — raw timestamps and measured durations. Observed primary serving RTO: 12 minutes 22 seconds (controller detection -> full request success). Metadata DB (multi-AZ sync) measured RPO: 3 minutes 8 seconds. KV-store rehydration note: warm-key recovery sub-60s; cold-key rehydration depends on background rebuild and is operationally best-effort (typical completion within 10–30 minutes in our test profile).
- Failover-Run-logs-20261015.log — controller logs (sanitized) with event ids and epoch timestamps.
- KV-Recovery-Snapshot-20261015.json — snapshot manifest and GUIDs.
- Tabletop-Exercise-Notes-20261015.txt — attendee list (ops, SRE, product), scenario notes, and three open action items (two completed, one in progress).

Caveats / notes for auditor:
- Private deployments: customers that self-host have different RTO/RPO behaviours depending on local storage and network topology; we documented the variations in Annex B of the runbook.
- Embeddings service uses asynchronous write-behind to the vector store in some Dedicated tiers — replication lag can result in RPO measured in minutes for cold writes; we call this out explicitly in the matrix.

Related references: JIRA DR-2026-119 contains the task run details; HubSpot HS-4321 links this evidence to Arcadia's security intake.

If the auditor would like raw UTC timestamps exported as a CSV for ingestion, Marissa can produce that by EOD Dec 2. Otherwise we'll walk through the provided XLSX during the call.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.
